node.label: Henri Lefebvre
node.date_label: 1968: Le Droit à la ville (first volume) · 1974: La production de l’espace (French book) · 1974: La production de l’espace (introduction excerpt, L’Homme et la société) · 1991: The Production of Space (translated by Donald Nicholson-Smith)
node.description: A philosopher and social theorist of everyday life, urban change and the social production of space. His spatial analysis asks how practices, competing forms of capital and hegemonic power actively produce space, rather than treating it as a passive setting or readable code.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Le Droit à la ville (first volume) (1968); La production de l’espace (French book) (1974); La production de l’espace (introduction excerpt, L’Homme et la société) (1974); The Production of Space (translated by Donald Nicholson-Smith) (1991).
node.scope_note: Selected theoretical contributions and dated texts, with original, revised, translated and posthumous forms distinguished. people_update.identity_note: Author of La production de l’espace (Anthropos, 1974), identified as Henri Lefebvre (1901–1991) in BnF record FRBNF35199294; English translation credited to Donald Nicholson-Smith by CiNii Books BA12992226. Distinct from Georges Lefebvre; no authority QID, biography node or automatic dissertation crosswalk. Revision 1.185 promotes this same Henri Lefebvre identity to a curated individual entry; any reading-link integration must be explicitly reviewed and is not an automatic dissertation crosswalk. proposed_edges.relationship: Treats social space as produced through practices and power, beyond inventories or textual decoding alone.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own 1974 introduction excerpt, pp. 19–20 reread; conceptual resource for spatial history, with historical reconstruction and GIS kept distinct.

proposed_edges.relationship: Examines space as an active medium in the conflicting operations of capital and class hegemony.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own excerpt, pp. 21–22 reread: distinguishes forms of capital and refuses to make capitalism a closed, contradiction-free system. This is Lefebvre’s theoretical intervention, not a verified general law of capitalist history.
